content.value: Schema v2 is the field-type system that gives every Schema its vocabulary — scalars, references, and the crucial `arrayOf` distinction.

Schema v2 defines what kinds of values a Document field may hold. Beyond plain scalars (string, number, boolean, datetime), the type that matters most for Barkpark's graph story is the Reference Field: a pointer from one Document to another. A reference comes in two shapes — a single scalar reference, or an
split is not cosmetic. The Edge Extractor must know which fields are
references so it can fan a single field out into multiple edges in the Content Graph. Get this wrong and edges silently vanish or double.
That awareness flows straight into Blast Radius analysis: when you change or delete a Document, every
reference that named it must be considered, not just scalar ones. The same applies to

field severs exactly one edge while leaving the others intact, whereas clearing a scalar reference removes the whole link. A correct Content Edges Table depends on Schema v2 modelling this faithfully.

Field types declared under Schema v2 drive form widgets in LiveView Studio, column types in the Go TUI, and the facet derivation behind Search Facets. Body fields typed as PortableDoc carry block trees rather than flat text. The whole type system is owned by the Phoenix API and self-described through the Capabilities Manifest so the bp CLI and JS SDK can validate inputs before a mutation ever reaches the HTTP API v1. Content plugins like OnixEdit and the Frt plugin add their own fields on top of this same vocabulary rather than inventing a parallel one.
